newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures benefited on Friday from a virtuous combination of weak unemployment figures, an intervention rate cut and European Union acceptance of the French government plan to reduce its 1997 public deficit.
The December contract reached a high for the week at 126.62 after the EU announcement before drifting lower to settle at 126.44, little changed from 126.48 last Friday.
French bonds outperformed German bonds along the curve with the 10-year spread moving to minus four and the two-year spread narrowing to 22 basis points from 25 on Wednesday.

Economists said the EU decision had largely been discounted as had the Bank of France intervention rate cut. Although there was some disappointment the cut was only five basis points analysts said it meant there was still room for more cuts.
They said while a rate cut never hurts in difficult economic circumstances, it would have little effect on the economy.

"It is in many ways a symbolic cut because it's true the macroeconomic impact of such a small rate cut is not going to be major," Societe Generale economist Michala Marcussen said. "Basically the Bank of France is signalling that they are doing what they can do."
The franc, which climbed from 3.3767 as high as 3.3740 after the Telecom decision was announced but suffered late in the day after a Bundesbank council member said he thought the ruling was "wrong."
The franc fell back to 3.3765 per mark, still a long way above Tuesday's low of 3.3869 when concerns about the acceptability of the Telecom transfer resurfaced.

December PIBOR slipped slightly from the contract high of 96.48 it hit earlier on Thursday but settled at 96.47, up three basis points. It outperformed the Euromark contract with the spread narrowing to 32 basis points from 35.
French bond futures got an initial boost early on Thursday from weaker-than-expected French September unemployment figures which economists said highlighted the sluggishness of the domestic economy.
"This is really bad," said Credit Commercial de France economist Valerie Plagnol. "The worry is that there's a risk of still further deterioration."
